| 3.10       | First npm release: `render-svg` and `cli render`                       | ✅ done | [0053](../adr/phase-3-text/0053-what-linux-and-macos-said.md) — the release turned out to be a measurement: `pptx-studio render` has no canvas, so it reads the font tables itself, and fifteen probe fonts built to disagree with themselves were asked against Chromium - widths 540/540, kerning 90/90, the face box 30/30, the ideographic baseline 38/38, with 19 of 19 mutants dead. The face box has no one table: DirectWrite reads `usWin` and FreeType `hhea`, bit 7 moving both onto `sTypo`; CoreText reads `hhea` whatever bit 7 says and holds the em ratio as 16.16 fixed point before rounding half up, 94/94 on Linux and 248/248 on macOS, so the reader answers per rasteriser. Nothing had ever installed a published package, so the release gate now packs every tarball, installs it into a scratch consumer against a dead registry and runs the example; twelve packages are on npm with provenance, every version published without it is deprecated, and a scheduled canary opens and closes its own issue. | 3.11       | Gate 3's hundred slides, and what zoom does to them                    | ✅ done | [0054](../adr/phase-3-text/0054-a-hundred-slides-at-any-zoom.md) — PowerPoint was exported at seven widths and 266 cases settled seven families, each with one perfect fit and every hand-written alternative refuted: a hairline is one device pixel at every width (42/42), a stroke is its width rounded to whole pixels and never under one (56/56), a dashed hairline is solid, a pattern tile is six points at every width, text scales linearly and gradients are identical from 480 px. So zoom is a fresh mount at that width, never a resize, and `stroke-width` and `stroke-dasharray` were the only bytes of the markup that could differ until a line end's numbers and a crisp path's translate joined them. `a46-hundred-slides` (100 generated slides, oracle at 120/240/960/1920/3840 px) hit every limit nothing had reached - the one-byte grid count, the per-file and total corpus caps, a quadratic deck reload, a Linux baseline that could not grow - and found two defects: every bordered picture was blank and no bullet was drawn. `pnpm gate3` drives the studio page itself in Chromium, takes it offline, and screenshots every slide at every zoom against PowerPoint: 100 slides, 500 rasters, all drawn, all invariant, no request after going offline; by zoom 9954/9878/9960/9964 bp and 9727 for the 120-px strip. A rotated glow in an EMU-unit filter cost Chromium nine seconds a shape; written in points it is thirty milliseconds and the strip of a hundred thumbnails takes 761 ms. A real hundred-slide deck went through the page unscored and needed nothing fixed. Finishing it found that no renderer had ever drawn a line end: the six heads are drawn now, from F2's pen (M8, 49/49), and the gate's mask owns a head's numbers as it owns `stroke-width`. A 2x display is measured too: switched to unannounced, the page's 100 % is the 200 % markup to the byte on every slide and its redrawn strip the 25 % markup on every thumbnail, its rasters within 5 levels of 255 of the 200 % rasters; and PowerPoint's own exports at 240 and 120 px agree with its 960 export at 9879 and 9742 bp where the page's columns are 9878 and 9727. Then F3 asked where an edge lands: 1498 cases at up to four sub-pixel offsets settled that a stroke's centre rounds half up and an odd pen sits on pixel centres (732/732 on lines, rectangles, a custom L, a triangle's base and a quarter turn), fill and picture edges round half up (192/192), a border sits half its true width outside the rounded frame (48/48), a slant snaps at its endpoints (24/24) and a curve adds a quarter-pixel bias of its own; a pen of an exact half pixel rounds up at 480 and 960 and down at 1200 and no rounding fits both. The renderer draws rectilinear paths crisp with an odd pen moved half a device pixel, the gate's mask owns that move, a named height stretches as the export does, and 75 corpus slides moved toward PowerPoint (corpus mean 9841 → 9844 bp; 25 % 9878 → 9897, the strip 9727 → 9749). A fourth pass ran F3 at fourteen widths, 3388 cases, to close what the third left open: the half pixel rounds up at 240, 480, 960 and 1920 and down at 1200, and no integer-EMU width is a half at 3840, so the renderer’s rounding is right at every zoom the page has; an algn="in" stroke, never measured before, is the device pen a pixel outside the rounded frame edge and the rest inside (48/48); every case fits the rule on the six widths that are an eighth of a pixel per point with a whole-pixel height, 239 and 227 of 242 fit at 1040 and 1120 where an exact half rounds width and parity apart off the powers of two (1040, 1120, 1200), a fractional height moves the rows by the stretch in quarter-pixel steps with the columns intact (140/150 at 1320), and a fractional dots per inch — a41-a4 at 960 is one — is a resampled render that snaps no row, which is that slide’s basis point. A rectangular picture’s border is now the pen on the frame outset by half the width, over the picture, crisp where the width is whole pixels, with no clip; the twelve bordered slides moved 2–4 bp each and the strip 9749 → 9753. 28/28 mutants killed, then 23/23, then 13/13, then 11/11. |
| 3.12       | The public website, from npm, on GitHub Pages                          | ✅ done | [0055](../adr/phase-3-text/0055-the-website-installs-what-it-documents.md) — the example became `website/`: a static Next export with Fumadocs docs for all twelve packages, a live demo of each and a playground that takes a visitor's own deck, installed from the registry, never the workspace, so the site is at most one release behind and never ahead of what npm serves. The candidate gate, the canary and the deploy run the same four scripts from the same manifest and differ only in where the packages come from; a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow (`9625cca` has no run), so the deploy follows the release on `workflow_run` and waits for the registry to serve every range before it installs. The CLI renders eleven corpus decks (144 slides, 6.1 s) at build, the API reference is read from each installed `dist/index.d.ts`, and thirteen typed snippets fail the gate on a renamed export. The export is walked in Chromium under the Pages base path before upload: the Worker's bootstrap and four chunks load, a deck fetches, a slide mounts, the search index answers, and first load is 218/239/202/203 kB gzipped on the landing, a docs page, the viewer and the playground. Two mutants killed, one killed once the smoke test counted decks against its manifest, one shown equivalent; the first deploy (run 34780332460, 140 s to build and walk, 9 s to deploy) served every route, deck, index and Worker chunk under the base path with nothing at or above 400, and a PowerPoint-authored deck dropped on the live playground was censused, validated and exported, and the export opened in the real PowerPoint with no repair. The site's first review found the editor demo unusable - three edits behind a form, refusing a shape whose fill or position it inherited - so it is now direct manipulation over four gestures on the slide: drag, colour, type where the text is drawn, delete, each writing what PowerPoint writes for the same gesture, a local override placed by `insertInOrder`, with undo the exact inverse; eleven planner tests over the 144 shipped slides hold every edit in schema order and byte-identical on undo, seven edited downloads opened in PowerPoint with no repair, and the first dragged placeholder found V028 mistaking `a:xfrm/a:ext` for an extension, fixed in validate. Lighthouse 13.4.1 before the review: mobile 76/71/56 and desktop 100/92/85 for performance on the landing, a docs page and the playground, 96-97 accessibility on a contrast defect since fixed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Carried debt

Open across sub-phases, and not owned by any of them.

### `packages/validate` is still at 1.2's 29 rules

Four text sub-phases each identified rules that belong in the repair firewall and none were added: `p:kinsoku/@lang`, three `bodyPr` rules, `@panose` shape, and `@u`/`@strike` simple types.

Raised in: ADR 0029, ADR 0032, ADR 0033, ADR 0034.
